paper.citation: Hu S. et al. (2013) Comparison of the inhibition mechanisms of adalimumab and infliximab in treating tumor necrosis factor alpha-associated diseases from a molecular view. J Biol Chem 288:27059-27067

user_supplied_pdf.note: The student supplied the publisher PDF locally. It is gitignored and never committed; no text extractor was available on this machine, so the transcription came from the PMC rendering of the same article and was then spot-checked against the PDF by the student.

spot_check.note: Two rows were read back from the PDF and agree with this record exactly, including the printed errors. The remaining rows are not independently confirmed against the PDF.

table_3.title: Kinetics and binding affinity of TNF-alpha mutants with the adalimumab Fab
table_3.method_as_printed: Kinetics and affinity of TNF-alpha mutant and the adalimumab Fab were analyzed using a BIAcore T100. Wild type TNF-alpha and the mutants were passed over the immobilized adalimumab Fab surface, and the data were globally analyzed using a simultaneous fit for both dissociation (kd) and association (ka). The value for KD was calculated as kd/ka.
transcription_notes: The kd cell for P113A is printed as 1.394 +/- 0.209 x 10(3) s^-1. The printed KD and ka are self-consistent only with 1.394 x 10(-3); the exponent sign is missing in the rendering, so the negative exponent is recorded here.
The ka error for Q67A is printed as 2.557 +/- 3.383 x 10(4): the error exceeds the value. It is recorded exactly as printed and is not used in any comparison.
KD values are recorded as printed, not recomputed from ka and kd.

authors_own_conclusions_as_printed.quote: Notably, the mutant TNF Q21A presented a sharp decrease in the binding to Adalimumab with a 200-fold lower binding affinity. The same phenomenon was observed in the TNF K65A, TNF Q67A, TNF E135A, and TNF E146A mutations. All of these mutants resulted in a 100-200-fold affinity decrease.
authors_own_conclusions_as_printed.note: The authors' own residue labels in this passage use the numbering of Table 3, which matches the deposited 3WD5 author numbering.

authors_reported_interface.buried_surface_note: The Results state a total buried surface area of 2,540 A^2 for the Fab-TNF interface; the Discussion states 2,536 A^2 for one adalimumab Fab with trimeric TNF-alpha. Both are the authors' own values and neither is recomputed here.
authors_reported_interface.two_protomer_quote: The Adalimumab epitope on TNF-alpha is composed of a number of discontinuous segments, including residues ... and TNF Thr-71, TNF His-72, TNF Thr-77, TNF Thr-79, TNF Ser-81, TNF Lys-89 to TNF Asn-91, and TNF Glu-135 to TNF Asn-137 of an adjacent TNF-alpha protomer.
authors_reported_interface.cdr_claim_quote: Both the heavy and light chains of Adalimumab participated in the interaction with TNF-alpha, with all of the contacts coming from CDRs. CDRs L2 and H2 contribute to the majority of the interactions with the antigen.
authors_reported_interface.hydrogen_bond_claim_quote: Over 20 pairs of hydrogen bonds or salt bridges stabilized the TNF-alpha-Adalimumab Fab complex (Table 2).

epitope_residue_list_as_printed.numbering_note: Part of this printed list is offset by one relative to Table 3 and to the deposited 3WD5 coordinates: the printed Pro-19/Gln-20 and Thr-71/His-72 and Lys-89 to Asn-91 correspond to Pro20/Gln21, Thr72/His73 and Lys90 to Asn92 in Table 3 and in the coordinate file. The remaining listed residues match. This is recorded as an observation about the printed text, not a correction of the structure.

project_use: The mutation fold changes are the authors' measurements and are never presented as this project's results.
This project compares the authors' fold changes with its own geometric buried-surface values; that comparison is descriptive and establishes no causal or energetic relation.
The authors' reported total buried surface (2,540 A^2) is used as an independent cross-check of this project's symmetry reconstruction.
